unit: licence + insurance kept current in LauderBuild
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale accepts building permit applications only from contractors holding a current certificate of competence and licence in their field (Code Sec. 9-27), and every licensed professional has to register and keep licence and insurance documents current in LauderBuild. Expired credentials block permits and even fee payments, and expired licences drop out of the public search - so a contractor you cannot find there is worth a phone call before you sign.
detail_rows: City registration :: Online only, through LauderBuild - not by email or post: a registration form, a state licence or county certificate of competency, liability insurance, and workers' comp or an exemption letter, with the City of Fort Lauderdale, 700 NW 19th Avenue, as certificate holder - Contractors & Licensed Professionals page | Permits only to licensed contractors :: Applications for building permits are accepted only from contractors holding a current certificate of competence and license in their respective fields, apart from the exceptions in Secs. 9-28 and 9-29 - Code Sec. 9-27 | Business tax :: Before working, engaging in business or contracting in any listed classification, a contractor must pay any required local business tax and show the receipt on demand - Code Sec. 9-73 | Check them yourself :: In LauderBuild (aca-prod.accela.com/FTL) run a Licensed Professional Search, or Reports > LP License Status to see when their documents expire. Expired licences are not searchable at all | Minor work only :: The city lets non-licensed contractors register only for certain project types and minor construction work | County licence :: Broward's Building Code Division handles contractor licensing and enforcement under County Code Ch. 9 through the Central Examining Board of Construction Trades. County-licensed contractors, suspensions and revocations are checked by phone on 954-765-4400; complaints go to CLE-Complaint@broward.org | Marine cards are voluntary :: Broward lists its marine specialty, marine seawall, bulkhead, dock and pile-driving certificates under Division I (Voluntary), so a county card is not mandatory for marine work - Broward Contractor packet | State licence :: Search the company and the qualifier on DBPR's Verify a Licensee (myfloridalicense.com). A licence number starting with C is a state certification valid anywhere in Florida; one starting with R is a registration, good only where the holder met local competency rules - F.S. 489.105(8),(10) and the DBPR licensing page | Who may build a seawall or dock :: A certified general contractor's scope is unlimited (489.105(3)(a)). The state also certifies five marine specialties: marine specialty, marine seawall work, marine bulkhead work, marine dock work and marine pile driving - Rule 61G4-15.100(1)(b)-(f) | Workers' comp :: In construction a single employee makes coverage mandatory (440.02(20)(b)2). Up to three officers or LLC members owning at least 10% may file exemptions (440.02(18)(b)2), and the exemption certificate itself says it is not a DBPR licence (440.05(4)). Check it on the DWC data portal's Coverage and Exemptions search (dwcdataportal.fldfs.com) | Recovery fund :: For contracts signed on or after 1 July 2024 the Homeowners' Construction Recovery Fund pays at most $100,000 per claim against a Division I contractor (general, building, residential) and $30,000 against a Division II contractor, which includes the marine specialties; the lifetime caps are $2 million and $600,000 per licensee - 489.143(3),(6). unit: Civic Access account + state or county licence
qualifier: Miami Beach says contractors must be registered with the city to work in Miami Beach. State-certified contractors register with a business tax receipt from their Florida place of business; county-licensed contractors need a CTQB certificate of competency and a Miami Beach Municipal Contractors Tax Receipt. The code separately bars a contractor from starting work in the city without first giving the city manager proof of compliance with county contractor law and of workers' comp and liability cover (Sec. 18-276).

unit: DBPR contractors register online
qualifier: Key West's code requires every contractor working in the city to hold and keep a city licence, issued under the city's business tax receipt rules (Secs. 18-146, 18-147), and to hold a current certificate of competency for its trade (Sec. 18-150). DBPR state-licensed contractors register through an online form; specialty contractors need a competency card, and the city sends testing to Monroe County.
detail_rows: DBPR registration :: Online Licensed Contractor Registration Form: attach workers' comp or exemption, business tax receipts from the local jurisdiction, liability insurance and the DBPR state licence. The form reminds contractors that F.S. 489.119(5)(c) requires the registration or certification number on any vehicle bearing the company name | Specialty cards :: Specialty trades must show a competency card; the City does not test - call the Monroe County Contractor License Coordinator, (305) 289-2583 - Note on Specialty Contractors page | Homeowner permits :: An agent may not act for someone applying for a homeowner permit unless a licensed contractor is employed - Sec. 18-118(b) | Past permits :: eTRAKiT (etrakit.cityofkeywest-fl.gov) has Search Permit and Search Contractors pages | County certificates :: Monroe's Contractors Examining Board (County Code Secs. 6-263 to 6-270) issues certificates of competency, including Seawall & Small Dock (Marine Const.) Engineering Class II (c), which needs three years' experience. County certificate holders may work only where the county has a reciprocal agreement | County look-up :: Search county licences in MCeSearch (mcesearch.monroecounty-fl.gov) or call the Monroe County Licensing Coordinator, 305-289-2583 | State licence :: Search the company and the qualifier on DBPR's Verify a Licensee (myfloridalicense.com). A licence number starting with C is a state certification valid anywhere in Florida; one starting with R is a registration, good only where the holder met local competency rules - F.S. 489.105(8),(10) and the DBPR licensing page | Who may build a seawall or dock :: A certified general contractor's scope is unlimited (489.105(3)(a)). The state also certifies five marine specialties: marine specialty, marine seawall work, marine bulkhead work, marine dock work and marine pile driving - Rule 61G4-15.100(1)(b)-(f) | Workers' comp :: In construction a single employee makes coverage mandatory (440.02(20)(b)2). Up to three officers or LLC members owning at least 10% may file exemptions (440.02(18)(b)2), and the exemption certificate itself says it is not a DBPR licence (440.05(4)). Check it on the DWC data portal's Coverage and Exemptions search (dwcdataportal.fldfs.com) | Recovery fund :: For contracts signed on or after 1 July 2024 the Homeowners' Construction Recovery Fund pays at most $100,000 per claim against a Division I contractor (general, building, residential) and $30,000 against a Division II contractor, which includes the marine specialties; the lifetime caps are $2 million and $600,000 per licensee - 489.143(3),(6). Nothing is paid if the contractor was unlicensed when you signed - 489.141(2)(d) - and residential contracts over $2,500 must print the fund notice - 489.1425 | Deposits :: A contractor who takes more than 10% up front on residential work must apply for permits within 30 days and start within 90 days of the permits issuing, unless you agreed to longer in writing - 489.126(2)(a) | Three-day cancel :: If the deal was a home solicitation sale over $25 - signed away from the seller's place of business and not the result of your own request for specific goods or services - you can cancel in writing until midnight of the third business day; Sundays and federal holidays don't count - 501.021, 501.025 | Business tax is not a licence :: A contractor pays business tax where its permanent office is, and no other city or county may levy a business tax or an equivalent registration fee for temporary work there - 205.065
